newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Far East may import some grain - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Far East may import some grain - Interfax.

text.p: Russia will largely be able to meet its wheat needs this year, but grain is of low quality and Russia's Far East may continue imports as in recent years, a bread inspection official said on Tuesday.

In remarks quoted by Interfax news agency, State Bread Inspectorate deputy head Viktor Maltsev said Russian wheat output this year would rise to 32-24 million tonnes, including 16-18 million tonnes of food wheat, from last year's total output of 30.1 million tonnes.
"This is fully enough to satisfy the country's bread needs," he said. But at least five million tonnes of food wheat would be fed to livestock because it was of poor quality.
Maltsev said areas needing higher-quality supplies would look to other regions, including Orenburg and Osmk, while Russia's Far East might find it cheaper to import.

Russia's gross 1996 grain harvest is 74.6 million tonnes, according to preliminary official figures. No figures for wheat have been released, but independent specialists have put this year's wheat harvest at about 34 million tonnes.
The inspectorate had found 52,400 tonnes of out the 2.8 million tonnes of grain it inspected over the first nine months of this year unsuitable in terms of quality.
Russia has imported wheat every year over the past several years, but has not made single large purchases.
